transcript.answer:
Short answer
- thumb-api is exhausting its render worker pool and rejecting requests ("no free render worker within 1.0s (workers=4)"), causing 503 responses that the web-frontend logs show as repeated "thumbnail request failed: 503".
- The catalog-indexer is the dominant caller during the failure bursts and is responsible for the majority of thumb-api traffic and most of the failing requests. In a representative 2‑minute failure window (09:24–09:26 UTC) catalog-indexer generated ~1,048 of ~1,315 total requests (~79.8% of requests) and ~123 of ~145 of the 503 responses (~85% of failing requests).

What I looked at (evidence)
- Pods (namespace=media): thumb-api-58bcf947d5-lfs9m and web-frontend-7f757cc945-8pnfw.
- web-frontend logs (multiple timestamps) show repeated thumbnail request failures returning 503 over the 09:19–09:40 UTC interval (many lines like "2026-10-07T09:21:46Z ERROR web-frontend thumbnail request failed: 503").
- thumb-api logs show repeated worker rejections starting in the same interval: many WARN lines like:
  - "2026-10-07T09:21:25Z WARN render rejected: no free render worker within 1.0s (workers=4)"
  - Rejections continue repeatedly through the 09:21–09:40 window.
- Prometheus metrics discovered: thumb_requests_total (labeled by client and code), thumb_render_workers, thumb_inflight.
- Per-client, per-code traffic (2-minute windows) shows catalog-indexer traffic >> other callers during bursts; web-frontend and image-proxy are smaller contributors.

Prometheus graphs (request-rate and per-client counts)
<< {"type":"promql","tool_name":"execute_prometheus_range_query","tool_call_id":"call_vMeNg4dDjeAvFwvCeBnYeNZA"} >>

<< {"type":"promql","tool_name":"execute_prometheus_range_query","tool_call_id":"call_W2fjQyJ1lyIoRmNmWujdUKHf"} >>

Quantified example (representative 2‑minute window, 09:24–09:26 UTC)
- catalog-indexer (200): 925.55 reqs
- catalog-indexer (503): 123.13 reqs
- web-frontend (200): 133.56 reqs
- web-frontend (503): 17.74 reqs
- image-proxy (200): 86.61 reqs
- image-proxy (503): 3.13 reqs
- email-renderer (200): 24.00 reqs
- email-renderer (503): 1.04 reqs

Totals (same window)
- Total requests ≈ 1,314.8
- Catalog-indexer total ≈ 1,048.7 → 1,048.7 / 1,314.8 ≈ 79.8% of requests
- Total 503s ≈ 145.0; catalog-indexer 503s ≈ 123.1 → 123.1 / 145.0 ≈ 85.0% of failing requests

Root cause (confirmed + likely)
1. Confirmed: thumb-api is rejecting requests due to no available render worker slots (log message: "no free render worker within 1.0s (workers=4)"), producing 503s observed by callers.
2. Likely immediate trigger: very high request volume concentrated from catalog-indexer during the bursts (it accounts for ~80% of incoming requests and ~85% of failures in representative windows), which pushes the render worker pool to saturation.
3. System-level or design factor: render_workers is currently 4 per instance (log), which is too small for the incoming burst rate; thumb-api may also be under-provisioned (too few pods) or lacking queuing/backpressure for high-volume callers.

Actionable remediation (short- and medium-term)
Immediate (fast, low risk)
- Rate-limit or throttle the catalog-indexer so requests to thumb-api are smoothed (preferred short-term mitigation).
- Apply backoff/retry tuning on catalog-indexer if it retries aggressively.
- If catalog-indexer is configurable: batch thumbnail requests or move heavy jobs to off-peak windows.

Scale and config changes
- Increase the render worker pool (app config / env var controlling workers) — example check and patch:
  - Inspect deployment: kubectl -n media get deploy thumb-api -o yaml
  - If render_workers is an env var, increase it (edit deployment or Helm values) and rollout.
- Scale thumb-api horizontally (add replicas) while ensuring each pod has sufficient worker configuration:
  - kubectl -n media scale deployment thumb-api --replicas=<N>
  - Monitor thumb_render_workers and thumb_inflight after scaling.

Longer term / reliability improvements
- Add server-side queuing and a bounded request queue with backpressure (so callers receive 429 rather than saturating workers/triggering 503s).
- Add a circuit breaker on callers (catalog-indexer) so it reduces load when thumb-api rejects.
- Prioritize user-facing callers (web-frontend) over batch/internal callers (catalog-indexer) at thumb-api (request prioritization).
- Add/adjust alerts:
  - Alert when rate of "render rejected" (or thumb_requests_total{code="503"}) exceeds threshold.
  - Alert when thumb_inflight approaches total capacity or when occupied workers ~100%.

Suggested immediate monitoring/commands
- Watch rejected/warning logs: kubectl -n media logs -f deployment/thumb-api
- View per-client request rates (already present): thumb_requests_total grouped by client and code.
- After mitigation, re-check web-frontend logs for 503s and thumb-api logs for "render rejected" to confirm reduction.

Confidence and caveats
- Confirmed facts: the exact log lines in thumb-api and web-frontend and the per-client metrics with client labels (catalog-indexer, web-frontend, image-proxy, email-renderer).
- Interpretation: that catalog-indexer load is the dominant cause of bursts is supported by the per-client traffic numbers in multiple 2-minute windows; it is the most likely immediate caller responsible for saturating the workers. There could be additional contributing factors (CPU/memory limits, single-node scheduling, or a longer-running render queue) that I did not inspect; if you want, I can expand the investigation to:
  - check thumb-api pod resource usage (kubectl top pod) and deployment replica count,
  - inspect the deployment/Helm values for render_workers and autoscaling settings,
  - fetch more granular logs or longer time windows.

If you want I will:
- Increase the analysis window or pick more peak windows and produce a time series of the catalog-indexer share.
- Inspect deployment YAML/Helm values for thumb-api and suggest the exact env/Helm change.
- Provide a one-line kubectl/Helm change to increase workers and an exact rollout command. Which would you prefer me do next?
